title: Pinecrest Healthcare private deploy proposal (draft)
content:
Executive summary:

This is a draft customer-specific private deployment proposal for Pinecrest Healthcare (PHI workload). They requested a VPC/on-prem hybrid with dedicated inference capacity behind customer-managed networking and KMS integration for keys. This doc contains: sizing assumptions, proposed architecture diagrams (described), Terraform module notes for provisioning, an upgrade/rollout plan, open questions, and next-step action items.

High-level constraints and customer requirements (from kickoff):
- Regulated PHI — no plaintext data leaves the VPC.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM (Azure Key Vault / AWS CloudHSM compatible).
- On-prem compute for inference (primary) with optional cloud burst.
- 99.9% availability target for critical routes, 95th pct latency SLO 150ms for <512 token requests.
- Expected peak concurrency: 180 concurrent model sessions during business hours, 24x7 baseline 25 sessions.
- Max request size average 250 tokens; worst-case 2048 tokens for batch/rerank jobs.
- Maintenance windows allowed weekly 02:00–04:00 local.

Sizing proposal (initial):
- Serving fleet: 6 dedicated nodes (NVIDIA A10G-class equivalent), each configured as follows: 80GB vram effective after quantization + multi-instance support. Rationale: estimated 30 concurrent sessions per node for our optimized generation path at median length 250 tokens and batching limits. With 6 nodes we get 180 concurrent sessions headroom.
- CPU/Memory for control plane + routers: 3x m5.2xlarge-equivalent VMs (HA pair + standby) for the private control plane/agent services.
- Storage: 3x 1TB NVMe local per serving node for model shards + KV cache persistence.
- Caching: Redis cluster (3 nodes) for prefix cache invalidation and small key reads. Can be deployed inside customer VPC or via provided appliance.

Notes on model variants and fallback:
- Primary: quantized 4-bit variant of open LLM (customer approved model A).
- Fallback: smaller 8-bit variant on CPU for low-priority routes or during GPU exhaustion.
- Traffic shaping: route critical endpoints to dedicated node pool; non-critical to shared pool.

Network & security architecture (text description):
- Customer VPC contains subnets: control-plane-subnet, inference-subnet, infra-subnet (monitoring, redis).
- Private control plane services (console proxy, rollout manager) run in infra-subnet and connect to Redwood-managed management plane via restricted egress (TLS only) — optional based on customer acceptance.
- On-prem nodes run behind customer-managed NAT/load balancer; TLS mutual-auth to control plane.
- KMS integration: Redwood agent will call customer KMS via private endpoints (VPC endpoint or on-prem HSM gateway).

Terraform module notes (implementation hints / TODOs):
- Module: redwood.vpc (variables: cidr_block, az_count, nat_enabled boolean, private_subnet_prefixes). Outputs: vpc_id, private_subnets.
- Module: redwood.iam (variables: service_accounts, kube_role_bindings). Must support idempotent creation and custom allowed-roles mapping for customer auditors.
- Module: redwood.k8s-nodepool (variables: node_count, gpu_type, gpu_count_per_node, taints, labels). Templatize for multiple instance-types for cost/availability.
- Module: redwood.gpu-driver (job) — installs NVIDIA drivers, container toolkit, and sets MIG profiles (where applicable). Must run as DaemonSet for idempotent upgrade.
- Module: redwood/secret-backends - hooks for customer KMS (supports aws_kms, azure_keyvault, pkcs11-HSM). Provide a 'mock' mode for test environments.
- Module outputs and state: expose outputs for LB DNS, nodepool IDs, KMS key id, and a versioned module tag used for operator-side compatibility checks.

Recommended Terraform workflow for customer (notes to SEs):
- Create a bootstrap workspace that only provisions network, IAM, and KMS bindings (apply first).
- Second workspace provisions node pools (gpu) and infra (redis, monitoring).
- Third workspace deploys Redwood agents and services.
- Lock module versions in a registry/lockfile to control operator compatibility during upgrades.

Upgrade plan (rolling, minimize downtime):
1) Preflight: run 'redwood healthcheck' across control plane and node pools; run golden prompt set eval (smoke) against a staging node.
2) Canary: bring up 1 new node with target runtime version + agent; divert 5% of traffic. Monitor latency, error rates, mem/GPU metrics for 6 hours.
3) Gradual rollout: if canary stable, increment nodes by 1–2 (depending on cluster size) every 90 minutes; maintain autoscaling disabled for the duration.
4) Cache migration: warm Redis/cache on new nodes via prefix replays before shifting traffic to reduce cold-start spikes.
5) Fallback: automated rollback to prior runtime image triggered if 95th pct latency > +30% or error rate >2% for 10m.
6) Post-upgrade: run full eval harness and commit results to Confluence.

Specific migration considerations:
- KV cache format changes: ensure backward-compatibility flag or migration job that iterates keys and converts format.
- Tokenization differences: if model tokenizer updated, run a token-stability check on a 1k-sample corpus before cutting over.

Architecture Q&A (customer facing, draft):
Q: Can we keep keys entirely inside our HSM?
A: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Redwood agents will only receive short-lived material; private endpoints required.

Q: What happens if one entire AZ goes down?
A: With the node pool sizing above + cross-AZ placement & LB, we can tolerate single AZ failure with degraded throughput. We recommend autoscaling to absorb mid-size spikes post-failure.

Q: Are telemetry and logs forwarded outside the VPC?
A: No by default. We can push logs to a customer-managed Fluentd endpoint in infra-subnet or ship only aggregated metrics (no payloads) to Redwood console by customer opt-in.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Customer will provide physical GPU nodes or equivalent cloud instances that accept our nodepool bootstrap (bare-metal or VM).
- Network egress rules allow TLS-only connections from control plane agent to Redwood endpoints (if customer opts for managed-control-plane features).
- Customer accepts 4-week lead time for procurement of A100/A10G-class hardware + driver bake time.
- Model licensing/weights are provided by customer or approved public model.

Open questions / risks (items to resolve in next 2 weeks):
- Q1: Customer's exact cluster networking topology (flat VPC vs segmented hybrid) — ticket JIRA-PR-56 created.
- Q2: HSM vendor/version and PKCS#11 compatibility — need vendor doc and test access.
- Q3: Does customer require air-gapped installation? If yes, deliverable is separate offline-install tarball and on-prem engineer visit.
- Risk: older NVIDIA driver incompatibilities with quantized runtime; mitigations: preflight driver matrix test and offer managed driver image.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: draft Terraform bootstrap workspace templates for Pinecrest (due 2024-12-01).
- Diego: vendor-auth test plan for HSM (contact Pinecrest infra) (due 2024-11-22).
- Liam: prepare canary checklist + telemetry thresholds (due 2024-11-20).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-prem ops runbook (copyable to customer):
- Verify BIOS and driver versions per GPU compatibility matrix.
- Confirm kernel modules and container runtime support (nvidia-container-toolkit).
- Install Redwood agent via signed package; verify mutual-TLS certificate exchange.
- Pre-pull model artifacts to local NVMe to avoid cold-start.
- Run golden prompt set and regression checks; capture token-level diffs.

Notes / rough thoughts (internal):
- Consider adding a lightweight 'edge appliance' for customers who want single-box installs (saves a lot of operator time during onboarding).
- Terraform modules should emit telemetry tags (customer-id, env, module-version) for easier debugging and audit.
- Make a small 'upgrade-safe' flag in nodepool module that sets PodDisruptionBudgets and minimizes rolling-churn.

References and links: Confluence draft (internal) https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Pinecrest+On-Prem+Kickoff, internal PR with terraform examples git@github.com:redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pinecrest, JIRA-1234 (KMS integration), JIRA-PR-56 (network topology).

End of draft. Please review and drop inline comments. This doc will be converted to a one-page customer proposal and a separate internal install runbook once the open questions are closed.
